views.note: xml_loc=60: payment.provider form inheritance (APS merchant identifier / access code / SHA request & response phrases) + the QWeb redirect-form template payment_aps_templates.xml (auto-submit POST form to the PayFort payment page carrying command/access_code/merchant_identifier/merchant_reference/amount/currency/language/customer_email/signature[/payment_option]/return_url), plus data/payment_provider_data.xml wiring redirect_form_view_id. No own model views.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_specific_rendering_values -> hidden-field POST redirect to the PayFort payment page (https://checkout.payfort.com/FortAPI/paymentPage / sandbox https://sbcheckout.payfort.com/FortAPI/paymentPage)
behavioral_notes.observation: APS is a pure hosted-redirect acquirer: there is NO server-to-server payment API call. _get_specific_rendering_values builds a PURCHASE command payload (command='PURCHASE', access_code=aps_access_code, merchant_identifier=aps_merchant_identifier, merchant_reference=tx.reference, amount=to_minor_currency_units(amount,currency) as a string, currency=currency.name, language=partner_lang[:2], customer_email=partner.email_normalized, return_url=base_url+/payment/aps/return) and, for non-'card' methods, a payment_option mapped by utils.get_payment_option (the card brand upper-cased, e.g. VISA; 'card' is omitted so the buyer picks the brand on the PayFort page). It then signs the whole dict via provider._aps_calculate_signature(rendering_values, incoming=False) and adds api_url=provider._aps_get_api_url() (live vs sandbox by provider.state). These values feed the redirect_form QWeb template whose hidden inputs auto-POST the browser to PayFort's hosted payment page. The acquirer endpoint, the PURCHASE command, and the signed-form handoff are invisible to Python model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider._aps_calculate_signature -> SHA-256 signing with separate request/response phrases
behavioral_notes.observation: _aps_calculate_signature implements PayFort's signature scheme: it concatenates 'key=value' for every data item EXCEPT 'signature', sorted by key, with no separator, then sandwiches that string between the SHA phrase on both sides (signing_string = phrase + sorted_pairs + phrase) and returns hashlib.sha256(signing_string).hexdigest(). The phrase is direction-dependent: aps_sha_request for OUTGOING (Odoo->APS, incoming=False, used when building the redirect form) and aps_sha_response for INCOMING (APS->Odoo, incoming=True, used in the controller to verify the return/webhook). This dual-phrase, sandwich-style SHA-256 (not an HMAC) is pure code semantics, not derivable from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: APSController.aps_return_from_checkout (/payment/aps/return, POST) + aps_webhook (/payment/aps/webhook, POST) -> _verify_signature(incoming) BEFORE _process; reference via _extract_reference -> merchant_reference
behavioral_notes.observation: Both public, csrf=False POST routes follow the identical guarded pattern: _search_by_reference('aps', data) (routing through _extract_reference -> data['merchant_reference']) locates the tx, then _verify_signature is called BEFORE _process. _verify_signature reads data['signature'] and rejects with werkzeug Forbidden (HTTP 403) when it is missing or when hmac.compare_digest(received, provider._aps_calculate_signature(data, incoming=True)) fails -- a constant-time compare against the SHA-256 recomputed with the response phrase. The return route additionally carries save_session=False (so a SameSite-less session cookie is not lost on the cross-site POST) and redirects to /payment/status; the webhook returns '' to acknowledge. Both ultimately call tx_sudo._process('aps', data), which validates the amount (via _extract_amount_data) then runs _apply_updates. Unlike most acquirers the return route here is itself authenticated and authoritative (it is a POST carrying the signed feedback), so APS does not depend on a separate verification GET.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._apply_updates -> APS status -> payment state mapping
behavioral_notes.observation: _apply_updates stamps provider_reference = payment_data['fort_id'], resolves the payment method from payment_data['payment_option'].lower() via payment.method._get_from_code (falling back to the current method), then maps APS' numeric status through const.PAYMENT_STATUS_MAPPING into payment's guarded transitions: '19' -> _set_pending; '14' -> _set_done; a missing status -> _set_error('missing payment state'); any other status -> _set_error carrying payment_data['response_message']. There is no _set_canceled branch -- cancellations surface as the error fallback. _extract_amount_data converts payment_data['amount'] back from minor units via to_major_currency_units and returns currency_code=payment_data['currency'] for the engine's amount cross-check. This inbound status->state translation is pure code, not visible in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, signing phrases, no API key
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=false; the only declared endpoints are the two PayFort hosted payment pages -- https://checkout.payfort.com/FortAPI/paymentPage (live) and https://sbcheckout.payfort.com/FortAPI/paymentPage (sandbox) -- selected by provider.state in models/payment_provider.py (_aps_get_api_url). There is NO outbound REST client and NO bearer/api-key auth here: APS is reached purely by the browser POSTing the signed hidden-field form to the hosted page, and APS returns to Odoo's /payment/aps/return + /payment/aps/webhook. Authenticity rests entirely on the SHA-256 request/response phrases (aps_sha_request / aps_sha_response) + access code, not on a transport-level key. This redirect-only acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of the PayFort endpoints, the PURCHASE command, or the phrase-based signing are reachable from model/field metadata.

0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches (gap #3). payment_aps ships no client-side code: the entire buyer interaction is the server-rendered redirect_form QWeb template (payment_aps_templates.xml) whose hidden inputs auto-submit to PayFort. There is therefore no browser SDK and no inline card form -- the card data is collected on PayFort's hosted page, never in Odoo. The only browser-visible artifact is the auto-POST redirect form, which is itself plain server-rendered HTML (no gap-#3 JS surface).

it_architecture.application: payment_aps (Amazon Payment Services / PayFort acquirer adapter for the payment engine; _inherit-only, no own models/views)
software_services: /payment/aps/return (redirect-return, http POST, csrf=False, save_session=False: signature-verified, processes the signed feedback, then /payment/status)
/payment/aps/webhook (async notification, http POST, csrf=False: signature-verified, processes, returns '')
data_objects: payment.transaction (APS hosted-redirect PURCHASE flow; no new fields; 5 override methods)
logical_data_erm: payment.transaction -> payment.provider (provider_id; provider_code=='aps' gates every override)
external: payment.transaction.reference == APS merchant_reference (cross-system key for return/webhook lookup via _extract_reference)
information_flows: depends: payment (inherits the provider/transaction engine + redirect-form rendering + _process state machine)

outbound (redirect): _get_specific_rendering_values -> signed hidden-field POST form -> browser auto-submit to https://checkout.payfort.com/FortAPI/paymentPage (sandbox sbcheckout.payfort.com) -- no server-to-server API call
inbound (return): APS -> POST /payment/aps/return -> _verify_signature (SHA-256 response phrase, constant-time compare) -> _process -> /payment/status
inbound (webhook): APS -> POST /payment/aps/webhook -> _verify_signature -> _process -> payment state machine
no tokenization / no refund / no capture / no void flows in this module
frontend_components: redirect_form QWeb template (payment_aps_templates.xml; server-rendered hidden-field auto-POST form to the PayFort payment page; no JS/OWL)

external_integrations.sdk: none (no python SDK and no browser SDK; card data entered on PayFort's hosted page, never in Odoo)
external_integrations.auth: no transport key; authenticity via SHA-256 sandwich signature with direction-specific phrases -- aps_sha_request (outgoing) / aps_sha_response (incoming) -- plus aps_access_code & aps_merchant_identifier in the signed payload
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration, but in its simplest hosted-redirect form. There is NO outbound REST/API-key channel -- the browser POSTs a server-signed hidden-field form to PayFort's hosted payment page (live or sandbox by provider.state), the buyer pays on PayFort, and APS returns the signed feedback to /payment/aps/return and /payment/aps/webhook, both verified by recomputing the SHA-256 signature with the response phrase. The base 'payment' engine ships no live acquirer; this module is exactly that override, contrasting with Stripe/Xendit by being redirect-only (no S2S API, no tokenization).
external_integrations.note: Gap-#7 example with no API key: none of the PayFort endpoints, the PURCHASE command, or the dual-phrase SHA-256 signing are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py + const.py + utils.py.

capabilities: Accept Card payments via Amazon Payment Services (PayFort) hosted redirect across the MENA region
Accept specific card brands (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover) -- mapped to APS payment_option, or let the buyer choose the brand on the hosted page
Signed-redirect settlement (SHA-256 request/response phrases) with no card data ever touching Odoo
Multi-currency acceptance (no module-side currency allow-list; bounded by the payment.method/PayFort account configuration)
value_streams: Collect-Payment (redirect): initiate tx -> _get_specific_rendering_values builds the signed PURCHASE form -> browser auto-POST to the PayFort payment page -> buyer pays on PayFort -> POST /payment/aps/return (signature-verified) AND/OR async POST /payment/aps/webhook -> _process -> state machine pending/done/error
Settle: status '14' -> _set_done -> downstream post-process settlement (account_payment / sale)
information_concepts: payment.provider (APS/PayFort credentials: merchant identifier, access code, SHA request phrase, SHA response phrase)
payment.transaction (mapped to an APS PURCHASE; keyed by merchant_reference=reference, provider_reference=fort_id)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; aps_access_code / aps_sha_request / aps_sha_response are restricted to base.group_system; aps_merchant_identifier and everything else inherit payment's groups/record rules)
policies: Inbound authenticity: return and webhook data must pass _verify_signature (SHA-256 sandwich with aps_sha_response, constant-time hmac.compare_digest) or are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden
Outbound redirect-form integrity: the form is signed with aps_sha_request before the browser POSTs it to PayFort
References are forced to a singularized 'tx'-prefixed token (_compute_reference) so document names (e.g. INV/2020/...) never leak disallowed characters into APS' merchant_reference
Amounts are sent in minor currency units (to_minor_currency_units) and read back via to_major_currency_units
Access code / SHA phrases gated by base.group_system field groups
stakeholders: Merchant / Company (res.company, holds the APS/PayFort merchant account, access code & SHA phrases)
Amazon Payment Services / PayFort (external acquirer / PSP for the MENA region)
Accountant (consumes settled payments via account_payment downstream)
metrics: (no own reports; transaction volumes/amounts/state surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_aps is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the MENA-region cardholder/payer and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Amazon Payment Services' (PayFort's) card network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (merchant identifier, access code, and SHA request/response phrase management; per-brand payment-method enablement), service provisioning (building and signing the per-transaction PURCHASE redirect and confirming the signed feedback), and infrastructure operation (the hosted-redirect handoff to the PayFort payment page plus the signature-verified return/webhook settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its APS realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe / payment_xendit metamodels (network/support) and the parent payment engine; APS is the thinnest variant -- a redirect-only acquirer with no server-to-server API and no tokenization.

standard_capabilities: hosted-redirect card payment via the Amazon Payment Services (PayFort) payment page (PURCHASE command, live vs sandbox by provider.state)
per-brand payment-method routing (Visa / Mastercard / Amex / Discover) via the APS payment_option, or buyer brand-choice on the hosted page
signed-redirect integrity and signature-verified settlement via SHA-256 request/response phrases
asynchronous settlement via a signature-verified webhook plus an (also signature-verified, POST) redirect-return route
multi-currency acceptance (minor-unit amounts; currency from the transaction, no module-side allow-list)
typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting card payments in the MENA region via Amazon Payment Services / PayFort
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
merchants needing card acceptance without holding card data (SAQ-A: PayFort-hosted page, nothing entered in Odoo)
brand-specific routing where the merchant pre-selects Visa/Mastercard/Amex/Discover as activatable methods
common_gaps: no server-to-server API: only the hosted-redirect PURCHASE flow is implemented (no direct/S2S charge, no inline form)
no tokenization / saved cards (no _extract_token_values, no off-session recurring) -- every payment is a fresh redirect
no manual capture / authorize-then-capture, no void, and no in-module refund operation (no _send_capture/void/refund_request override)
no explicit cancel state mapping (only '19'->pending and '14'->done; everything else, including cancellations, falls through to _set_error)
the public-URL requirement for the return/webhook means local/dev instances need a tunnel; without the SHA response phrase set, signature verification has no secret to compare against
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here

open_questions: Exact APS / PayFort hosted-page request and transaction-feedback field sets beyond those built in _get_specific_rendering_values / read in _apply_updates (fort_id, status, payment_option, response_message, amount, currency).
Real-world distribution of APS transaction states and brand mix (card vs Visa/Mastercard/Amex/Discover) -- no runtime row counts captured.
How refunds / cancellations are handled operationally given no in-module refund override and no cancel-state mapping (likely via the PayFort dashboard or a downstream module).
Whether instances reliably register the webhook vs rely on the (also signed) POST return route, and whether both can fire for the same transaction.
